subproblem.title: Integer median with Poincaré and boundary estimates for integer-valued functions on the unit cube (the BV facts of Simon 6.5.1, (26)–(33))
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} (Euclid n, Lebesgue measure), and div G := trace of the derivative (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). There is c > 0, depending only on m, such that: if u : ℝⁿ → ℝ is integer-valued (u(y) ∈ ℤ for every y), integrable on Q₁, and V ∈ ℝ satisfies ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y, then there is β ∈ ℤ with (1) ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ cV, (2) |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|, and (3) |∫_{Q₁}(u − β) · div G| ≤ cV for every C^∞ map G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with |G(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ m : ℕ, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (V : ℝ), (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, u y = z) → IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, u y * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y) ≤ V) → ∃ β : ℤ, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - β| ≤ c * V ∧ |(β : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y| ∧ ∀ G : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) G → (∀ y, ‖G y‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, (u y - β) * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G y)| ≤ c * V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the BV facts that Simon uses on the n-faces in displays (26)–(33) of the proof of 5.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 1844–1900). He cites Ch. 6, 2.34–2.35 and Ch. 2, 2.7, 2.9: the Poincaré inequality for BV functions on a cube, the choice (31) of an integer median β_F, and the boundary estimate (32). Here these facts are proved directly for an integer-valued integrable u on the open unit cube, by mollification, a smooth Poincaré inequality and a trace inequality, so no BV theory is needed. Conclusion (3) is the boundary-mass estimate M(∂((u − β)[[Q₁]])) ≤ cV of (32) written without currents: the field G represents an (n − 1)-form. The frozen statement is byte-identical to that of cmcdt_cube_bv_median (compactness_of_minimizing_currents branch, speculative-ready) and of dtc_bc_lc_fd_dfm_cube_bv_median (local_comparison branch, a single-theorem leaf in formalization); neither is accepted, so a fresh name is used, and an accepted single-theorem proof of the latter can be transplanted verbatim (no dependencies). The argument below is the one written and reviewed for that statement.

Notation. n := m + 1 ≥ 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ ℝⁿ (Lebesgue measure Lⁿ, Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1), div G := trace DG. For 0 < δ < 1/8, Q_δ := (δ, 1 − δ)ⁿ (side s = 1 − 2δ ∈ [3/4, 1]). φ ∈ C_c^∞(B_1(0)), φ ≥ 0, ∫φ = 1, φ_σ(z) := σ^{−n}φ(z/σ), φ̌_σ(z) := φ_σ(−z). ū := u·1_{Q₁} ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), u_σ := ū ∗ φ_σ ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ). Let u, V be as in the statement.

0. Preliminaries. Taking g = 0 gives V ≥ 0. Applying the hypothesis to g and −g gives |∫_{Q₁} u div g| ≤ V for every admissible g (smooth, compact support in Q₁, |g| ≤ 1). For every constant β and admissible g, ∫_{Q₁} β div g = 0 (integrate each ∂_i g_i along lines; g has compact support in Q₁). Hence v := u − β is integrable on Q₁ and satisfies the same hypothesis with the same V.

1. Gradient bound: for 0 < σ < δ < 1/8, ∫_{Q_δ} |∇u_σ| ≤ V. For g ∈ C_c^∞(Q_δ; ℝⁿ) with |g| ≤ 1, Fubini and differentiation under the convolution give ∫ ∇u_σ · g = −∫ u_σ div g = −∫ ū (φ̌_σ ∗ div g) = −∫_{Q₁} u div(φ̌_σ ∗ g). Here φ̌_σ ∗ g is smooth with compact support in Q_δ + B_σ(0) ⊆ Q₁ and |φ̌_σ ∗ g| ≤ 1, so the right side is ≤ V by 0. The supremum of ∫ ∇u_σ · g over such g equals ∫_{Q_δ}|∇u_σ|: take g_k := χ_k ∇u_σ/(|∇u_σ|² + 1/k)^{1/2} with smooth cut-offs 0 ≤ χ_k ≤ 1, χ_k ↑ 1_{Q_δ}, and use monotone convergence. This proves the bound.

2. Smooth Poincaré inequality. For a cube Q' of side s ∈ [1/2, 1] and v ∈ C¹(closure Q'), ∫_{Q'} |v − v_{Q'}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n ∫_{Q'} |∇v|, where v_{Q'} is the mean. Indeed |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 |∇v(x + t(y − x))| dt for x, y ∈ Q'. Integrate over Q' × Q'; for t ≤ 1/2 substitute x ↦ (1 − t)x + ty (Jacobian (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}, image ⊆ Q' by convexity), and for t ≥ 1/2 substitute y ↦ (1 − t)x + ty (Jacobian tⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}). This gives ∫∫ |v(x) − v(y)| dx dy ≤ √n s · 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫_{Q'} |∇v|. Since |v(x) − v_{Q'}| ≤ s^{−n}∫_{Q'}|v(x) − v(y)| dy, ∫_{Q'} |v − v_{Q'}| ≤ √n s 2ⁿ ∫_{Q'}|∇v| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n ∫_{Q'}|∇v|.

3. Poincaré inequality for u: ∫_{Q₁} |u − u_{Q₁}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V. By 1 and 2 (Q' = Q_δ), ∫_{Q_δ}|u_σ − (u_σ)_{Q_δ}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V for σ < δ. As σ ↓ 0, u_σ → ū in L¹(ℝⁿ) (continuity of translation in L¹: ‖ū ∗ φ_σ − ū‖₁ ≤ sup_{|h|≤σ}‖ū(· − h) − ū‖₁, and translation is continuous in L¹ because continuous compactly supported functions are dense in L¹(ℝⁿ) — simple functions are dense (Mathlib MemLp.exists_simpleFunc_eLpNorm_sub_lt), indicators of Borel sets of finite measure are approximated by continuous compactly supported functions by regularity of Lebesgue measure and Urysohn (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_lt_add, Set.exists_isOpen_lt_add, exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isCompact) — and these are uniformly continuous), so ∫_{Q_δ}|u − u_{Q_δ}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V. As δ ↓ 0, u_{Q_δ} → u_{Q₁} and ∫_{Q_δ}|u − u_{Q_δ}| → ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| by dominated convergence.

4. Integer median (C2). Since u is real-valued and integrable, Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ c}) → 1 as c → +∞ and → 0 as c → −∞. Let β be the least integer c with Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ c}) ≥ 1/2. Then Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) ≥ 1/2 and, since u is integer-valued, Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≥ β}) = 1 − Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β − 1}) > 1/2.
 (a) β minimizes c ↦ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c|. For c > β, |u − c| − |u − β| ≥ c − β on {u ≤ β} and ≥ −(c − β) on {u > β}, so ∫(|u − c| − |u − β|) ≥ (c − β)(Lⁿ{u ≤ β} − Lⁿ{u > β}) ≥ 0. The case c < β is symmetric, using Lⁿ{u ≥ β} ≥ 1/2. With c = u_{Q₁} and 3: ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V.
 (b) If β > 0 then u ≥ β on a set of measure ≥ 1/2, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ β/2. If β < 0 then u ≤ β on a set of measure ≥ 1/2, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ |β|/2. Hence |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

5. Trace estimate. Let G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be smooth with |G| ≤ 1, and let w ∈ L¹(Q₁) satisfy the hypothesis of the statement with the constant V. Then |∫_{Q₁} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w|.
 Proof. Let w_σ := (w 1_{Q₁}) ∗ φ_σ, σ < δ. Apply the divergence theorem on the box Q_δ to the smooth field w_σG, whose divergence is ∇w_σ · G + w_σ div G. (By Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus in each coordinate, ∫_{Q_δ} ∂_i(w_σG_i) = ∫ over the two faces {x_i = 1 − δ}, {x_i = δ} of ±w_σG_i; the Mathlib divergence theorem on boxes is not in the frozen import closure and is not needed.) This gives ∫_{Q_δ} w_σ div G = −∫_{Q_δ} ∇w_σ · G + ∫_{∂Q_δ} w_σ G · ν dH^{n−1}, so |∫_{Q_δ} w_σ div G| ≤ ∫_{Q_δ}|∇w_σ| + ∫_{∂Q_δ}|w_σ|. On the face {x₁ = δ}, |w_σ(δ, x')| ≤ |w_σ(x₁, x')| + ∫_δ^{1−δ}|∂₁w_σ(t, x')| dt for x₁ ∈ (δ, 1 − δ). Averaging over x₁ (length s ≥ 1/2) and integrating in x' gives ∫_{face}|w_σ| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|w_σ| + ∫_{Q_δ}|∇w_σ|; the same holds for all 2n faces. With 1 applied to w: |∫_{Q_δ} w_σ div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|w_σ|. Let σ ↓ 0 (w_σ → w 1_{Q₁} in L¹, and div G is bounded on closure Q₁), then δ ↓ 0 (dominated convergence): |∫_{Q₁} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w|.

6. Conclusion. Put c := 2^{n+1}√n + (2n + 1) + 4n·2^{n+1}√n > 0 (depending only on m). By 4(a), ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V ≤ cV, which is (1); 4(b) is (2). By 0, w := u − β satisfies the hypothesis with V, so by 5 and 4(a), for every smooth G with |G| ≤ 1, |∫_{Q₁}(u − β) div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n·2^{n+1}√n V ≤ cV, which is (3). ∎
proof_key_steps: V ≥ 0, |∫u div g| ≤ V, and u − β satisfies the same hypothesis.
Mollified u_σ satisfies ∫_{Q_δ}|∇u_σ| ≤ V (duality with fields φ̌_σ ∗ g supported in Q₁).
Smooth Poincaré on cubes of side in [1/2, 1] and the limits σ ↓ 0, δ ↓ 0 give ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V.
The least integer β with Lⁿ{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2 is a median (integer values), minimizes c ↦ ∫|u − c| and satisfies |β| ≤ 2∫|u|.
Divergence theorem and the elementary trace inequality on Q_δ give |∫_{Q₁} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫|w|; apply to w = u − β.

subproblem.title: Isoperimetric filling of integer multiplicity cycles in positive codimension from the scaled deformation theorem (Simon 6.6.1)

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 6.1 (Isoperimetric Theorem) and its proof (chapter-06.txt lines 1939–1961, printed pp. 168–169): apply the scaled deformation theorem 5.3 to the cycle with ρ chosen so that ρ^{m+1} exceeds the mass bound of the polyhedral part. This is step 7 of the parent's supplied proof. Departures from the printed text: (a) Simon states M(R)^{(n−1)/n} ≤ cM(T) with n the dimension of R; the frozen statement records the equivalent explicit bounds M(Y) ≤ cρz with ρ = (2cz)^{1/(m+1)} and the support bound inherited from (DTr); (b) the trivial case is z = M(Z) = 0 (not T = 0), handled by ρ = 1 and the fact that a current of zero mass vanishes. The same argument, for the all-dimension finite-net antecedent, is the accepted proof of Submission.cbr_isoperimetric_filling; that declaration has a different antecedent, so its proof is adapted rather than reused.

Notation. (DTr) is the displayed hypothesis. All currents are on univ in ℝ^P. For a test form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| with |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm). M(X) = M_{univ}(X) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over admissible ω (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω), and currents with equal values are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).

1. Fix P, m with m + 1 < P. (DTr) gives c₀ ∈ ℝ≥0 with c₀ ≥ 1 and the deformation property for this (P, m). Put c := c₀ (as a real number); then c ≥ 1, and this c depends only on (P, m).

2. Elementary facts.
 (a) M(0) = 0: every value of the zero current is 0, so every term ofReal(0(ω)) = 0.
 (b) spt 0 = ∅: every x lies in the open ball B_1(x), whose closure is compact and on which 0 vanishes, so x belongs to the zero region of 0.
 (c) |tα| = |t||α| for t ∈ ℝ and a covector α (the coefficients scale by t, and √(t²Σa²) = |t|√(Σa²)).
 (d) A current X with M(X) = 0 is 0. Let ω be a test form. x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous (a square root of a finite sum of squares of continuous coefficient functions) and has compact support, so it is bounded by some C ∈ ℝ. Put s := (|C| + 1)⁻¹ > 0. For t ∈ {s, −s}, the form tω is admissible: |tω(x)| = |t||ω(x)| ≤ s(|C| + 1) = 1 by (c). Hence ENNReal.ofReal(X(tω)) ≤ M(X) = 0, i.e. X(tω) ≤ 0. By linearity X(sω) = sX(ω) and X(−sω) = −sX(ω), so sX(ω) ≤ 0 and −sX(ω) ≤ 0, whence sX(ω) = 0 and X(ω) = 0 (s ≠ 0). Thus X = 0.

3. Let Z be integer multiplicity with compact support, ∂Z = 0 and M(Z) < ∞, and put z := M(Z).toReal ≥ 0, so M(Z) = ENNReal.ofReal z. Choose ρ > 0 with cz < ρ^{m+1} and (z = 0 or ρ = (2cz)^{1/(m+1)}):
 - if z = 0, take ρ := 1, so cz = 0 < 1 = ρ^{m+1};
 - if z > 0, take ρ := (2cz)^{1/(m+1)} > 0 (rpow of a positive number); then ρ^{m+1} = 2cz (Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow with 1/(m+1) = ((m+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹) and 2cz > cz because cz > 0.

4. Apply (DTr) (step 1) with this ρ and T := Z. Its hypotheses hold: Z is integer multiplicity, spt Z is compact, M(Z) < ∞, and M(∂Z) = M(0) = 0 < ∞ by (a). We obtain Q, R, S with R integer multiplicity, Z − Q − S = ∂R, (Q = 0 or ρ^{m+1} ≤ M(Q)), M(Q) ≤ cM(Z), M(R) ≤ cρM(Z), M(S) ≤ cρM(∂Z) and spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ thickening(3√Pρ, spt Z).

5. S = 0: M(S) ≤ cρM(∂Z) = cρ·0 = 0, so M(S) = 0 and S = 0 by (d).

6. Q = 0: otherwise ENNReal.ofReal(ρ^{m+1}) ≤ M(Q) ≤ c·ENNReal.ofReal z = ENNReal.ofReal(cz), so ρ^{m+1} ≤ cz (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff, cz ≥ 0), contradicting step 3.

7. ∂R = Z: for every ω, ∂R(ω) = (Z − 0 − 0)(ω) = Z(ω) − 0 − 0 = Z(ω).

8. Put Y := R. It is integer multiplicity and ∂Y = Z (step 7).
 - Case z = 0: M(R) ≤ cρ·ENNReal.ofReal 0 = 0, so R = 0 by (d). Then M(Y) = 0 ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(c(2cz)^{1/(m+1)}z) (every ENNReal is ≥ 0), and spt Y = spt 0 = ∅ by (b), which is contained in any set.
 - Case z > 0: ρ = (2cz)^{1/(m+1)}, and M(Y) = M(R) ≤ c·ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)·ENNReal.ofReal(z) = ENNReal.ofReal(cρz) = ENNReal.ofReal(c(2cz)^{1/(m+1)}z), using ENNReal.ofReal_mul (c ≥ 0, cρ ≥ 0) and ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal. Finally spt Y = spt R ⊆ spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ thickening(3√P(2cz)^{1/(m+1)}, spt Z) by step 4.
 In both cases Y has all required properties, with the constant c ≥ 1 of step 1, which depends only on (P, m). ∎

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (26)–(37) (chapter-06.txt lines 1844–1928, printed pp. 167–168), together with the finite family of polyhedral chains of 7.2 (1)–(3) (lines 2047–2091). The BV facts used by Simon on the faces (2.34–2.35; Ch. 2, 2.7, 2.9) are replaced by the sibling dtc_bc_tc_cl_dfm_cube_bv_median (CB). Simon bounds the variation on a face by μ_{∂Q}(F̆). Here the corresponding number is Var_F := M_{N_F}(∂Q₀) for explicit pairwise disjoint open neighbourhoods N_F, which needs no measure representation of ∂Q₀ (below, V_F denotes the coordinate n-plane of F). The frozen statement is byte-identical to that of cmcdt_face_replacement (compactness_of_minimizing_currents branch, speculative-ready) and of the leaf dtc_bc_lc_fd_dfm_face_replacement (local_comparison branch, in formalization), whose dependency CB has the same frozen type as ours; neither is accepted, so a fresh name is used, and an accepted single-theorem proof of the leaf can be transplanted after renaming CB. The argument below is the one written and reviewed for that statement.

Notation. n := m + 1. (VO), (MR), (IMC) are the three displayed hypotheses (frozen types of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub). Currents are on univ in ℝ^P; |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm, ‖ω‖ := sup|ω(x)|, and |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖. Support facts: spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B, spt ∂A ⊆ spt A, spt 0 = ∅, and a current vanishing on all test forms supported off a closed set E has support in E. Hⁿ := μHE[n], Lⁿ is Lebesgue measure, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ.

1. Trivial case n > P. Every n-covector on ℝ^P vanishes (n vectors in ℝ^P are linearly dependent), so every n-current is 0. Take c := 1 and 𝒬₀ := {0}; for Q₀ = 0 take Pc := 0 (0 and ∂0 = 0 are integer multiplicity, all masses are 0, spt 0 = ∅). From now on n ≤ P; let c_B be CB's constant and c := max(2, 1 + c_B).

2. Faces. For I = {i_1 < ⋯ < i_n} ⊆ {1,…,P} and b ∈ ℤ^P, F = F(b, I) := {x : b_i ≤ x_i ≤ b_i + 1 (i ∈ I), x_i = b_i (i ∉ I)} is an n-face; distinct pairs (b|_{all}, I) give distinct faces. Further notation:
 - F̆ := {b_i < x_i < b_i + 1 (i ∈ I), x_i = b_i (i ∉ I)}, Π_F := {x : x_i = b_i (i ∉ I)}, V_F := span{e_i : i ∈ I};
 - e_F is the n-vector α ↦ α(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) (a unit orientation of V_F);
 - φ_F(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{i_j} is an affine isometric embedding ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with φ_F(Q₁) = F̆ and φ_F([0,1]ⁿ) = F;
 - p̃_F(x) := (x_{i_j} − b_{i_j})_j and p_F := φ_F ∘ p̃_F (orthogonal projection onto Π_F);
 - δ_F(y) := dist(y, F ∖ F̆) = min_j min(y_{i_j} − b_{i_j}, b_{i_j} + 1 − y_{i_j}) for y ∈ F̆.
 Hⁿ⌞Π_F is the image of Lⁿ under φ_F (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so Hⁿ(F̆) = Hⁿ(F) = 1 and Hⁿ(F ∖ F̆) = 0; diam F = √n. The union of the n-faces is L_n = {x : at least P − n integer coordinates}. L_{n−1} (at least P − n + 1 integer coordinates) is the union of the (n−1)-faces and has Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0 (each (n−1)-face is covered by k^{n−1} sets of diameter √n/k, so its Hⁿ measure is ≤ C k^{n−1}k^{−n} → 0). L_n ∖ L_{n−1} is the disjoint union of the F̆ (for x with exactly P − n integer coordinates, I := the others, b_i := ⌊x_i⌋ (i ∈ I), b_i := x_i (i ∉ I)). Face currents: [[F]](ω) := ∫_F ⟨ω, e_F⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{[0,1]ⁿ} ω(φ_F y)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) dy is a current (|[[F]](ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖) with spt [[F]] ⊆ F.
 Lemma 2.1: if y ∈ F̆ and G ≠ F is an n-face, then dist(y, G) ≥ δ_F(y). (The same statement and proof hold verbatim for distinct j-faces of any common dimension j; it is used for j = n − 1 in 8.) Proof: let z ∈ G. Then |y − z| ≥ |y − p_F(z)|. If p_F(z) ∉ F̆ then |y − p_F(z)| ≥ δ_F(y). Otherwise the coordinates z_i (i ∈ I) are non-integers, so they are free coordinates of G. As G has exactly n free coordinates, they are I, and z_i ∈ (b_i, b_i + 1) forces G = F(b', I) with b'_i = b_i (i ∈ I). G ≠ F gives b'_k ≠ b_k for some k ∉ I, and |y − z| ≥ |b_k − b'_k| ≥ 1 ≥ δ_F(y).
 Neighbourhoods: N_F := {x : p_F(x) ∈ F̆, |x − p_F(x)| < δ_F(p_F(x))/2} is open.
 (i) N_F ∩ L_n ⊆ F̆: if x ∈ N_F ∩ G for an n-face G ≠ F, then y := p_F(x) ∈ F̆ satisfies |x − y| < δ_F(y)/2 ≤ dist(y, G)/2 ≤ |x − y|/2, which is impossible. So x ∈ F ⊆ Π_F and p_F(x) = x ∈ F̆.
 (ii) N_F ∩ N_{F'} = ∅ for F ≠ F': with y := p_F(x), y' := p_{F'}(x), Lemma 2.1 gives |y − y'| ≥ max(δ_F(y), δ_{F'}(y')), while |y − y'| < (δ_F(y) + δ_{F'}(y'))/2.
 Finite family. Given K (compact) and Λ, let 𝔉_K be the set of n-faces contained in cthickening(√P, K), a finite set (a bounded set contains finitely many unit faces), and 𝒬₀ := {Σ_{F∈𝔉_K} β_F[[F]] : β : 𝔉_K → ℤ, Σ_F|β_F| ≤ 2Λ}, where Σβ_F[[F]] is the current ω ↦ Σβ_F[[F]](ω). 𝒬₀ is finite (the image of a finite set of coefficient vectors) and does not depend on Q₀.

3. Decomposition on open faces (Simon (33)). Let Q₀ be as in the statement, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep and μ := R.measure. By (MR), μ(W) = M_W(Q₀) for open W, so μ(ℝ^P) = M(Q₀). By (VO), μ(ℝ^P ∖ spt Q₀) = 0, hence μ(ℝ^P ∖ L_n) = 0; and μ(L_{n−1}) = 0 as Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0. Thus Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_F F̆) = 0 (θ ≥ 1 on M). Let 𝔉 := {F : F̆ ∩ spt Q₀ ≠ ∅}. Since spt Q₀ ⊆ K is compact, 𝔉 is finite; every F ∈ 𝔉 lies in cthickening(√n, spt Q₀) ⊆ cthickening(√P, K) (so 𝔉 ⊆ 𝔉_K); and μ(F̆) = 0 for F ∉ 𝔉. For F ∈ 𝔉, (IMC)(b) with E := F̆ (Borel) gives a current A_F represented by R_F := (M ∩ F̆, θ, ξ). For every test form ω, the function θξ(ω) is Hⁿ-integrable on M (|ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω‖ a.e. by (IMC)(d), and ∫_M θ dHⁿ = μ(ℝ^P) = M(Q₀) < ∞). Splitting the representing integral over the disjoint sets M ∩ F̆ (F ∈ 𝔉) and the Hⁿ-null remainder gives Q₀(ω) = Σ_{F∈𝔉} A_F(ω) for all ω, and M(Q₀) = Σ_{F∈𝔉} μ(F̆).

4. Orientation on faces (Simon (26)–(27)). Fix F ∈ 𝔉. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F̆ there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ F̆) x Q_x and ξ(x) a unit orientation of Q_x (R_F is an IMRep). Since M ∩ F̆ ⊆ Π_F ∋ x, blowUpMap x r '' (M ∩ F̆) ⊆ V_F for all r > 0. Suppose Q_x ≠ V_F; pick q ∈ Q_x ∖ V_F, ε := dist(q, V_F)/2 and f(y) := max(0, ε − |y − q|). Then ∫_{blowUpMap x r''(M∩F̆)} f dHⁿ = 0 for all r, while ∫_{Q_x} f dHⁿ ≥ (ε/2)Hⁿ(Q_x ∩ B_{ε/2}(q)) > 0, contradicting the definition. So Q_x = V_F and, by the sign rule (two unit orientations of one n-plane differ by a sign: the transition between orthonormal bases has determinant ±1), ξ(x) = ±e_F. Let α_F be the n-covector with α_F(v_1,…,v_n) := det((v_j)_{i_k})_{j,k}, so e_F(α_F) = 1, and s_F(x) := ξ(x)(α_F) (a.e. ±1). Define u_F := s_Fθ on {x ∈ M ∩ F̆ : s_F(x) ∈ {±1}} and u_F := 0 elsewhere (Borel after modification of ξ on a null set; integer-valued). Then A_F(ω) = ∫_{F̆} u_F ⟨ω, e_F⟩ dHⁿ and ∫_{F̆}|u_F| dHⁿ = μ(F̆). With ũ_F := u_F ∘ φ_F (integer-valued on ℝⁿ, integrable on Q₁, ∫_{Q₁}|ũ_F| = μ(F̆)): A_F(ω) = ∫_{Q₁} ũ_F(y) ω(φ_F y)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) dy.

5. Boundary variation on a face (Simon (27)–(33)). For F ∈ 𝔉 let Var_F := M_{N_F}(∂Q₀) ≤ M(∂Q₀) < ∞ (a number; not to be confused with the plane V_F). Claim: ∫_{Q₁} ũ_F div g ≤ Var_F for every smooth g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support in Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1.
 Let ε_j := (−1)^{j−1} dx^{i_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{i_{j−1}} ∧ dx^{i_{j+1}} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{i_n}. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(N_F), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, with χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of the compact set φ_F(spt g) ⊆ F̆ ⊆ N_F, and put γ(x) := χ(x) Σ_j g_j(p̃_F x) ε_j. Then γ is a test (n−1)-form with tsupport γ ⊆ N_F and |γ(x)| = χ(x)|g(p̃_F x)| ≤ 1. For x ∈ F̆, ⟨dγ(x), e_F⟩ = Σ_j ∂_{i_j}(χ·g_j∘p̃_F)(x) = div g(p̃_F x): where g∘p̃_F ≠ 0 near x, χ = 1 near x; elsewhere both sides vanish; and derivatives in directions k ∉ I do not pair with e_F. For an n-face G ∈ 𝔉, G ≠ F, the integrand of A_G(dγ) vanishes, because tsupport dγ ⊆ N_F and N_F ∩ Ğ ⊆ N_F ∩ L_n ∩ Ğ ⊆ F̆ ∩ Ğ = ∅. Hence ∂Q₀(γ) = Q₀(dγ) = A_F(dγ) = ∫_{Q₁} ũ_F div g. Since γ is admissible for M_{N_F}(∂Q₀), ∫_{Q₁} ũ_F div g ≤ Var_F.
 Moreover Σ_{F∈𝔉} Var_F ≤ M(∂Q₀). For ε > 0 choose admissible γ_F with tsupport γ_F ⊆ N_F and ∂Q₀(γ_F) ≥ Var_F − ε. Since the N_F are pairwise disjoint, Σ_F γ_F is admissible (at each point at most one term is nonzero), so M(∂Q₀) ≥ Σ_F Var_F − |𝔉|ε.

6. Integer medians (Simon (31)–(32); CB). For F ∈ 𝔉 apply CB to ũ_F and the real number V := Var_F (finite, as Var_F ≤ M(∂Q₀) < ∞; CB's hypothesis is the claim of 5). There is β_F ∈ ℤ with (1) ∫_{Q₁}|ũ_F − β_F| ≤ c_B Var_F, (2) |β_F| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|ũ_F| = 2μ(F̆), and (3) |∫_{Q₁}(ũ_F − β_F) div G| ≤ c_B Var_F for every smooth G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with |G| ≤ 1. Put β_F := 0 for F ∉ 𝔉.

7. The polyhedral current (Simon (34)–(37)). Pc := Σ_{F∈𝔉} β_F[[F]]. Σ_F|β_F| ≤ 2Σ_F μ(F̆) = 2M(Q₀) ≤ 2Λ and 𝔉 ⊆ 𝔉_K, so Pc ∈ 𝒬₀. Since Hⁿ(F ∖ F̆) = 0,
 (Q₀ − Pc)(ω) = Σ_{F∈𝔉} ∫_{Q₁} (ũ_F − β_F)(y) ω(φ_F y)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) dy.
 (34a) For admissible ω, |ω(x)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n})| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 (one coefficient), so M(Q₀ − Pc) ≤ Σ_F ∫|ũ_F − β_F| ≤ c_B Σ_F Var_F ≤ c_B M(∂Q₀).
 (34b) For an admissible (n−1)-form γ', let α := φ_F^#γ' and G_F(y)_j := (−1)^{j−1} α(y)(e_1,…,ê_j,…,e_n) = (−1)^{j−1} γ'(φ_F y)(e_{i_1},…,ê_{i_j},…,e_{i_n}). G_F is smooth and |G_F(y)|² ≤ |γ'(φ_F y)|² ≤ 1 (distinct coefficients of γ'). By the coordinate formula for d (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply) and the chain rule, dγ'(φ_F y)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) = div G_F(y). Hence ∂(Q₀ − Pc)(γ') = (Q₀ − Pc)(dγ') = Σ_F ∫_{Q₁}(ũ_F − β_F) div G_F, which has absolute value ≤ c_B Σ_F Var_F ≤ c_B M(∂Q₀) by (3). So M(∂(Q₀ − Pc)) ≤ c_B M(∂Q₀).
 (36), (37) M(Pc) ≤ Σ_F|β_F| ≤ 2M(Q₀) (indeed M(Pc) = Σ|β_F|, see 8). ∂Pc = ∂Q₀ − ∂(Q₀ − Pc), so M(∂Pc) ≤ (1 + c_B)M(∂Q₀).

8. Integrality and the mass dichotomy. Pc is represented by the IMRep with carrier C_P := ⋃_{β_F≠0} F̆ (Borel, and countably n-rectifiable as a finite union of subsets of the affine images φ_F(ℝⁿ)), multiplicity |β_F| on F̆ (the F̆ are disjoint) and orientation sign(β_F)e_F. Approximate tangent space: for x ∈ F̆ and δ < δ_F(x), Π_F ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ F̆ (points of Π_F within δ_F(x) of x have their free coordinates strictly inside (b_i, b_i + 1)), and by Lemma 2.1 no other open face meets B_δ(x). So C_P ∩ B_δ(x) = Π_F ∩ B_δ(x), and for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0) and r < δ/ρ, ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' C_P} f dHⁿ = ∫_{V_F} f dHⁿ. That is, V_F is the approximate tangent space, oriented by sign(β_F)e_F. The action is Σ_F ∫_{F̆}|β_F| sign(β_F)⟨ω, e_F⟩ dHⁿ = Pc(ω). By (MR), M(Pc) = Σ_F |β_F| Hⁿ(F̆) = Σ_F |β_F|; hence either all β_F = 0 and Pc = 0, or M(Pc) ≥ 1.
 Boundary: for an (n−1)-form γ, Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus on [0,1]ⁿ give [[F]](dγ) = Σ_j (−1)^{j−1}([[G_j^1]](γ) − [[G_j^0]](γ)). Here G_j^ε is the (n−1)-face of F with x_{i_j} = b_{i_j} + ε, and [[G]](γ) := ∫_G ⟨γ, e_G⟩ dH^{n−1} with its coordinate orientation e_G (for n = 1, [[G]](γ) = γ(v) at the vertex G = {v}). So ∂Pc = Σ_G γ_G[[G]], a finite sum over (n−1)-faces with γ_G ∈ ℤ. It is integer multiplicity by the same construction in degree n − 1 (for n − 1 = 0: finite carrier of vertices, multiplicity |γ_v|, orientation sign(γ_v), approximate tangent space {0} at isolated points, H⁰ the counting measure).

9. Supports (Simon (23)).
 - spt Pc ⊆ ⋃_{β_F≠0} F. β_F ≠ 0 gives F ∈ 𝔉 (μ(F̆) ≥ |β_F|/2 > 0 by (2)), so F̆ meets spt Q₀ and F ⊆ cthickening(√n, spt Q₀) ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt Q₀).
 - spt(Q₀ − Pc) ⊆ ⋃{F ∈ 𝔉 : ∫_{Q₁}|ũ_F − β_F| > 0}. For such F, (1) gives Var_F = M_{N_F}(∂Q₀) > 0, so some γ with tsupport γ ⊆ N_F has ∂Q₀(γ) ≠ 0; by (VO), N_F meets spt ∂Q₀. As spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n and N_F ∩ L_n ⊆ F̆, F̆ meets spt ∂Q₀ and F ⊆ cthickening(√n, spt ∂Q₀). Hence spt(Q₀ − Pc) ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂Q₀).
 - spt ∂Pc ⊆ spt ∂Q₀ ∪ spt ∂(Q₀ − Pc) ⊆ spt ∂Q₀ ∪ spt(Q₀ − Pc) ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂Q₀).

10. With c = max(2, 1 + c_B) ≥ 1 and the finite set 𝒬₀ of 2 (fixed before Q₀), Pc satisfies every conclusion: Pc ∈ 𝒬₀ (7), Pc and ∂Pc integer multiplicity (8), Pc = 0 or M(Pc) ≥ 1 (8), the mass bounds (7), and the support inclusions (9). ∎
proof_key_steps: Trivial case n > P; unit grid n-faces, face currents [[F]], the finite family of integer chains on faces in cthickening(√P, K) with Σ|β_F| ≤ 2Λ.
Disjoint open neighbourhoods N_F with N_F ∩ L_n ⊆ F̆ (distance lemma for distinct faces).
Q₀ = Σ_F Q₀⌞F̆ (MR, VO, Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0, IMC(b)); approximate tangent planes of subsets of Π_F are V_F, so Q₀⌞F̆ = ũ_F[[F̆]] with integer ũ_F.
Testing ∂Q₀ with forms built from fields g on the face gives ∫ũ_F div g ≤ Var_F := M_{N_F}(∂Q₀), and Σ_F Var_F ≤ M(∂Q₀).
CB yields integer medians β_F; Pc := Σβ_F[[F]] ∈ 𝒬₀ with M(Q₀ − Pc), M(∂(Q₀ − Pc)) ≤ c_B M(∂Q₀), M(Pc) ≤ 2M(Q₀), M(∂Pc) ≤ (1 + c_B)M(∂Q₀).
IMReps of Pc and ∂Pc (Stokes on cubes), M(Pc) = Σ|β_F| so Pc = 0 or M(Pc) ≥ 1; supports via spt Q₀ and Var_F > 0 ⇒ F̆ meets spt ∂Q₀.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.17–2.29 (chapter-06.txt lines 380–530) and 3.3–3.9 (lines 776–870). These are the tools of displays (11)–(25) of the proof of the deformation theorem 5.1: products with [[(0,1)]], smooth push-forward 2.23–2.24, the homotopy formula and mass estimate 2.25–2.27, the Lipschitz push-forward 2.29, and integrality of push-forwards of integer multiplicity currents 3.3–3.9. They are packaged as two operators push and homot for the sibling skeleton (dtc_bc_tc_cl_dfm_skeleton_deformation). The frozen statement and the dependencies (IMS = cmcdt_im_series, PT = ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae) are byte-identical to those of the leaf dtc_bc_lc_fd_dfm_lipschitz_pushforward_homotopy (local_comparison branch, in formalization, not accepted), so a fresh name is used and an accepted single-theorem proof of that leaf can be transplanted verbatim; the argument below is the one written and reviewed for that statement. Departures from the printed text: (a) Simon defines f_#T for integer multiplicity T and Lipschitz f by the integral formula 3.6 and uses, without proof, that it agrees with the limit 2.29; this agreement is proved in B4 below. (b) Simon's completeness theorem 3.13 is not used: integrality comes from the integral representation of Part B, whose final summation step is the sibling cmcdt_im_series. (c) In A4(f) a cut-off removes any assumption that G − F be bounded.

Conventions and available declarations. (VO), (MR), (REP), (IMC) denote the four displayed hypotheses of the statement. IMS is the sibling theorem Submission.cmcdt_im_series (an exact dependency of this leaf), applied to (VO), (MR), (IMC). PT is the sibling theorem Submission.ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae (an exact dependency of this leaf): for Lipschitz F : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, a Borel set B, m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| on B, and F differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B, for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B the approximate tangent space of F(B) at F(b) is range DF(b). The accepted candidate commit of PT (6ae39d3e) adds `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz` to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean (operator commit 58a0bf378 in its history), and the runtime merges the accepted candidates of a leaf's dependencies into the leaf's proof base before that base is pinned; so the following SimonGMT theorems (namespace Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02, all in the import closure of AreaLipschitz) are available here, for maps f : E → F between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces with Borel σ-algebras, Hausdorff measure μHE[finrank E]:
 (CR) area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero: μHE[finrank E](f '' {x | DifferentiableAt ℝ f x ∧ ¬Injective (fderiv ℝ f x)}) = 0 (any f);
 (ND) area_image_nondifferentiable_eq_zero: for Lipschitz f, μHE[finrank E](f '' {x | ¬DifferentiableAt ℝ f x}) = 0;
 (AF) weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn: for Lipschitz f, a measurable set s on which f is injective and g : F → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dμHE[finrank E] = ∫⁻_s ENNReal.ofReal(Jf(x)) g(f(x)) dx, where Jf(x) := areaJacobianAt f x = (fderiv ℝ f x).normDet (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet), with Jf(x)² = det(Df(x)*Df(x)) (areaJacobianAt_sq_eq_det_adjoint_comp) and Jf(x) = 0 iff Df(x) is not injective (areaJacobianAt_eq_zero_iff_not_injective); Jf is measurable (measurable_areaJacobianAt). For real-valued g with ∫_{f(s)}|g| < ∞ the same identity holds for Bochner integrals (apply (AF) to g⁺ and g⁻).
The accepted candidate of IMS (9b823b5) also contains kernel-checked helpers that may be used for routine steps: dtc_imrep_current (every IMRep represents a current), dor_ims_action_eq_integral, unit_orientation_norm_le_one, and cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density (an integer-valued density m on a Borel, countably n-rectifiable, locally Hⁿ-finite set N, oriented Hⁿ-a.e. by unit orientations of approximate tangent planes, yields an IMRep R with R.action(ω) = ∫_N m η(ω) dHⁿ).
Currents are on univ in some ℝ^N = Euclid N; 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) are k-currents and 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) test k-forms. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|, and for a k-vector ζ (a continuous linear functional on k-covectors) |ζ| := sup{ζ(α) : |α| ≤ 1}. NC_k(ℝ^N) is the set of X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with compact support, M(X) < ∞ and, if k ≥ 1, M(∂X) < ∞ (this is the statement's hypothesis IsCompact X.support, X.mass < ∞, boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞). NC is closed under differences: spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y and M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y) (directly from the definitions). |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ for every current (scale ω to be admissible). The zero current is integer multiplicity (empty carrier). Hᵏ := μHE[k]; on ℝᵏ = Euclid k, μHE[k] is Lebesgue measure Lᵏ.

1. Multilinear algebra.
(L0) For a k-covector β, k!|β|² = Σ_{i_1,…,i_k} β(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_k})² =: ‖β‖²_HS (each increasing tuple occurs k! times up to sign, and tuples with repeats vanish). ‖·‖_HS is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear form, hence invariant under orthogonal changes of basis, and so are |·| and the dual norm on k-vectors.
(L1) For linear A : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} and a k-covector β on ℝ^{N'}, |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k|β|; dually |Λ_kAζ| ≤ ‖A‖^k|ζ|, where ⟨β, Λ_kAζ⟩ := ⟨A^#β, ζ⟩. By (L0) it suffices to bound ‖·‖_HS. Replacing one slot of a multilinear form γ by A multiplies its HS norm by at most ‖A‖ (for fixed other arguments, Σ_i γ(Ae_i, …)² = |Aᵀg|² ≤ ‖A‖²|g|², g the vector representing γ(·, …)); do this k times.
(L2) For a 1-covector β' and a k-covector γ, |β' ∧ γ| ≤ |β'||γ| (rotate so that β' = |β'|e¹ and use (L0)). Dually |v ∧ ζ| ≤ |v||ζ| for a vector v and a k-vector ζ, where ⟨β, v ∧ ζ⟩ := ⟨ι_vβ, ζ⟩, and |ι_vβ| ≤ |v||β|.
(L3) If τ_1,…,τ_k are orthonormal then ζ := τ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_k (⟨α, ζ⟩ := α(τ_1,…,τ_k)) has |ζ| = 1. If A : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N is linear and injective, A = OS (S := (AᵀA)^{1/2}, O := AS^{−1} an isometric embedding). So Λ_kA(e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_k) = det(S)·Oe_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ Oe_k, |Λ_kA(e)| = √det(AᵀA) = (A).normDet, and Λ_kA(e)/|Λ_kA(e)| is a unit simple k-vector orienting A(ℝᵏ). If A is not injective, Λ_kA(e) = 0. Two unit simple k-vectors orienting the same k-plane differ by a sign (the change of orthonormal basis has determinant ±1). In particular, for G differentiable at u, |Λ_kDG(u)(e)| = JG(u) (notation of (AF)). By (IMC)(d), the orientation ξ of an IMRep satisfies |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.

Part A. Normal currents with compact support.

2. A0 (Representation). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) have compact support and M(X) < ∞. (REP) with U = univ gives a Borel measure μ_X and ξ_X with μ_X(W) = M_W(X) for open W, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X. Then μ_X(ℝ^N) = M(X) < ∞. Moreover μ_X(ℝ^N ∖ spt X) = M_{ℝ^N∖spt X}(X) = 0, because every admissible ω supported in the open set ℝ^N ∖ spt X has X(ω) = 0 by (VO). Hence |X(ω)| ≤ ∫ |ω| dμ_X, and X(ω) = 0 whenever ω vanishes on spt X.

3. A1 (Smooth push-forward). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) have compact support and F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be C^∞. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) put (F^#ω)(x) := ω(F(x)) ∘ DF(x) (Lean: (ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)), a smooth k-form. Put F_#X(ω) := X(ζF^#ω) for ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^N) equal to 1 on a neighbourhood of spt X; this does not depend on ζ (two choices differ by a form vanishing near spt X; (VO)).
 - F_#X is a current: if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) then ζF^#ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) by the chain and Leibniz rules (all derivatives of F are bounded on spt ζ).
 - ∂F_#X = F_#∂X: d commutes with F^# (SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with U = V = univ), so ∂F_#X(ω) = X(ζ d(F^#ω)) = X(d(ζF^#ω)) − X(dζ ∧ F^#ω). The last term vanishes by (VO) since dζ = 0 near spt X, and X(d(ζF^#ω)) = ∂X(ζF^#ω) = F_#∂X(ω) (ζ = 1 near spt ∂X ⊆ spt X).
 - spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X): if tsupport ω ∩ F(spt X) = ∅, then F^#ω vanishes on the open set F^{-1}(ℝ^{N'} ∖ tsupport ω) ⊇ spt X, so tsupport(ζF^#ω) ∩ spt X = ∅ and F_#X(ω) = 0 by (VO). F(spt X) is compact, and a current vanishing on all forms supported in the complement of a closed set E has support in E (each point outside E has a ball with compact closure disjoint from E).
 - If M(X) < ∞, A0 gives F_#X(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω(F(x)), Λ_kDF(x)ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X(x). Hence by (L1), |F_#X(ω)| ≤ ∫ ‖DF‖^k|ω∘F| dμ_X and M(F_#X) ≤ sup_{spt X}‖DF‖^k M(X).

4. A2 (Product with [[0,1]]). We work directly in ℝ^{N+1} = Euclid (N + 1), writing its points as (t, x) with t the coordinate of index 0 and x ∈ ℝ^N the remaining ones (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)); so no transport of currents is needed); e₀ := ∂_t. For a (k+1)-form ω on ℝ × ℝ^N let ω₁(t,x)(v_1,…,v_k) := ω(t,x)(e₀, (0,v_1),…,(0,v_k)) and ω₀ := ω − dt ∧ ω₁ (dt-free). For X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with compact support put ([[0,1]] × X)(ω) := X(∫_0^1 ω₁(t,·) dt) and ({s} × X)(ω) := X(i_s^#ω), i_s(x) := (s, x). The integrand is a smooth k-form with compact support (the projection of tsupport ω), and both are currents, with support in [0,1] × spt X and {s} × spt X respectively. Writing ω = dt ∧ ω₁ + ω₀, one has d(dt ∧ ω₁) = −dt ∧ d_xω₁ and dω₀ = dt ∧ ∂_tω₀ + d_xω₀, so (dω)₁ = ∂_tω₀ − d_xω₁. Integrating in t and using that d_x commutes with ∫dt,
 ∂([[0,1]] × X) = {1} × X − {0} × X − [[0,1]] × ∂X (k ≥ 1; for k = 0 the last term is absent).
If M(X) < ∞, A0 gives ([[0,1]] × X)(ω) = ∫_0^1∫ ⟨ω(t,x), e₀ ∧ ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X dt, so by (L2) M([[0,1]] × X) ≤ M(X); likewise M({s} × X) ≤ M(X). Hence for X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N), [[0,1]] × X ∈ NC_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with M(∂([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ 2M(X) + M(∂X).

5. A3 (Smooth homotopy formula). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) have compact support, and let H : ℝ × ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be C^∞ with H(t, x) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) for (t, x) in a neighbourhood of [0,1] × spt X, F, G smooth. Since ∂H_# = H_#∂ (A1 in ℝ^{N+1}) and H_#({s} × X) = (H ∘ i_s)_#X with H ∘ i_1 = G, H ∘ i_0 = F near spt X, A2 gives
 G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#([[0,1]] × X) + H_#([[0,1]] × ∂X) (last term absent for k = 0).
If M(X) < ∞: near [0,1] × spt X, DH(t,x)e₀ = (G − F)(x) and DH(t,x)(0,v) = ((1 − t)DF(x) + tDG(x))v. So Λ_{k+1}DH(e₀ ∧ ζ) = (G − F)(x) ∧ Λ_k((1 − t)DF + tDG)(x)ζ, and by A1, (L1), (L2)
 M(H_#([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ ∫ |G − F|(‖DF‖ + ‖DG‖)^k dμ_X ≤ sup_{spt X}|G − F| · sup_{spt X}(‖DF‖ + ‖DG‖)^k · M(X).

6. A4 (Lipschitz push-forward). Let X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N) and let F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be Lipschitz with constant Λ. Fix φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^N), φ ≥ 0, ∫φ = 1, spt φ ⊆ B̄_1(0) (a smooth bump from Mathlib exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset, divided by its integral), φ_σ(z) := σ^{−N}φ(z/σ). F_σ := F ∗ φ_σ, F_σ(x) := ∫ F(x − y)φ_σ(y) dy, is C^∞ (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left), Λ-Lipschitz (|F_σ(x) − F_σ(x')| ≤ ∫|F(x − y) − F(x' − y)|φ_σ(y) dy), so ‖DF_σ‖ ≤ Λ, and |F_σ − F| ≤ Λσ. Fix s ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with s(t) = t on [−1, 2] and s constant outside [−2, 3], so that s and s' are bounded. Apply A3 to F_σ, F_τ (H := F_σ + s(t)(F_τ − F_σ), smooth and globally Lipschitz because F_τ − F_σ is bounded by Λ(σ + τ)):
 |(F_σ)_#X(ω) − (F_τ)_#X(ω)| ≤ sup|F_σ − F_τ|((2Λ)^k M(X)‖dω‖ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)‖ω‖) → 0 (σ, τ ↓ 0).
So F_#X(ω) := lim_{σ↓0}(F_σ)_#X(ω) exists. Properties:
 (a) |F_#X(ω)| ≤ Λ^k M(X)‖ω‖ (A1 for F_σ). So F_#X is linear and sequentially continuous (‖ω_j‖ → 0 when ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k), i.e. a current, with M(F_#X) ≤ Λ^k M(X).
 (b) ∂F_#X = F_#∂X (A1 for F_σ; ∂X ∈ NC_{k−1} since ∂∂X = 0).
 (c) If F is C^∞ (and Lipschitz), F_#X agrees with A1: DF_σ → DF and F_σ → F uniformly on spt X, so by the representation in A1, (F_σ)_#X(ω) → F_#X(ω) (A1 sense). In particular id_#X(ω) = X(ζω) = X(ω) by (VO).
 (d) spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X): if tsupport ω ∩ F(spt X) = ∅ then, by compactness, tsupport ω ∩ F_σ(spt X) = ∅ for small σ, so (F_σ)_#X(ω) = 0 (A1).
 (e) If F, G are Lipschitz with constants ≤ Λ and |F − G| ≤ δ on spt X, then |F_#X(ω) − G_#X(ω)| ≤ δ((2Λ)^k M(X)‖dω‖ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)‖ω‖). (Apply A3 to F_σ, G_σ with sup_{spt X}|F_σ − G_σ| → sup_{spt X}|F − G|, then let σ ↓ 0.) In particular F_#X depends only on F|spt X. It is linear in X: F_#(X − Y) = F_#X − F_#Y for X, Y ∈ NC_k (true for each F_σ with a common cut-off ζ).
 (f) Homotopy formula. Let F, G be Λ-Lipschitz, X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N), and let Ĥ : ℝ × ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be any Lipschitz map with Ĥ(t,x) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) on [0,1] × spt X. Then
 G_#X − F_#X = ∂Ĥ_#([[0,1]] × X) + Ĥ_#([[0,1]] × ∂X) (last term absent for k = 0), and
 M(Ĥ_#([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ sup_{spt X}|G − F|·(2Λ)^k M(X).
 Proof. By (e) in ℝ^{N+1} (applied to the currents [[0,1]] × X and [[0,1]] × ∂X of NC, whose supports lie in [0,1] × spt X), the right sides do not depend on the choice of Ĥ. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^N), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of spt X, and let s be the function fixed above (s, s' bounded, s(t) = t on [−1, 2]). H_σ(t,x) := F_σ(x) + s(t)χ(x)(G_σ − F_σ)(x) is C^∞ and globally Lipschitz with a constant independent of σ ≤ 1. Indeed ∂_tH_σ = s'(t)χ(G_σ − F_σ) and D_xH_σ = DF_σ + s(t)(Dχ ⊗ (G_σ − F_σ) + χ(DG_σ − DF_σ)) are bounded, because s, s', χ, Dχ are bounded and G_σ − F_σ is bounded on the compact spt χ uniformly in σ ≤ 1. H_σ equals F_σ + t(G_σ − F_σ) near [0,1] × spt X, and converges uniformly to H := F + s(t)χ(G − F), which is Lipschitz and agrees with F + t(G − F) on [0,1] × spt X. By A3 for F_σ, G_σ:
 (G_σ)_#X − (F_σ)_#X = ∂H_{σ#}([[0,1]] × X) + H_{σ#}([[0,1]] × ∂X), M(H_{σ#}([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ sup_{spt X}|G_σ − F_σ|(2Λ)^k M(X).
 As σ ↓ 0, the left side converges weakly to G_#X − F_#X (definition). By (c), (e) in ℝ^{N+1}, H_{σ#}Y → H_#Y weakly for Y = [[0,1]] × X, [[0,1]] × ∂X. Boundaries converge weakly (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), and lower semicontinuity of mass (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) gives the estimate with sup_{spt X}|G − F|.

Part B. Integrality (Simon 3.3–3.9 and 3.2(2)). Throughout, X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N), k ≥ 1, is integer multiplicity, X = τ(M, θ, ξ) for an IMRep (M, θ, ξ). Replacing M by M ∩ spt X ((IMC)(b) with the closed, hence Borel, set E := spt X; the new IMRep still represents X because the removed part of the carrier carries no mass: by (MR) and (VO), ∫_{M∖spt X} θ dHᵏ = M_{ℝ^N∖spt X}(X) = 0), we may assume M ⊆ spt X, so Hᵏ(M) ≤ ∫_M θ dHᵏ = M(X) < ∞ (MR). We may also assume that the orientation ξ is Borel measurable: the IMRep only gives a.e. strong measurability with respect to Hᵏ⌞M, so replace ξ by a Borel function equal to it Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk); the orientation property still holds Hᵏ-a.e. on M and the action ∫_Mθ⟨ω, ξ⟩dHᵏ is unchanged, so the new triple still represents X. The multiplicity θ is already measurable.

7. B1 (Parametrization). There are countably many compact A_i ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz G_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N and κ_i > 0 such that: G_i is differentiable at every u ∈ A_i with DG_i(u) injective; |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| ≥ κ_i|u − v| on A_i; the sets G_i(A_i) ⊆ M are pairwise disjoint; and Hᵏ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0.
 Proof: by SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝᵏ), Hᵏ(M₀) = 0, F_j : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N Lipschitz. The differentiability set D_j of F_j is Borel (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt), Hᵏ(F_j(ℝᵏ ∖ D_j)) = 0 by (ND), and Hᵏ(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 for Z_j := {u ∈ D_j : DF_j(u) not injective} by (CR). Let E_j := (D_j ∖ Z_j) ∩ F_j^{-1}(M) (Borel). For injective A choose K_A > 0 with |Au| ≥ |u|/K_A (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith) and r(A) := 1/(2K_A) (r(A) := 1 otherwise). Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt covers E_j by disjoint Borel sets E_j ∩ t_l on which F_j approximates A_l = DF_j(y_l) (y_l ∈ E_j, so A_l is injective) with constant r(A_l); there |F_j(u) − F_j(v)| ≥ |u − v|/K_{A_l} − |u − v|/(2K_{A_l}) = (2K_{A_l})^{-1}|u − v|. Enumerate the pieces and make the images disjoint inductively, E'_i := E_i ∖ G_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i}G_{i'}(E'_{i'})), which is Borel by Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn. The union of the images contains M ∖ (M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝᵏ ∖ D_j) ∪ ⋃_j F_j(Z_j)), whose complement in M is Hᵏ-null. By inner regularity of Lebesgue measure, write each E'_i, up to an Lᵏ-null set N_i, as a countable disjoint union of compact sets; Hᵏ(G_i(N_i)) = 0 because Lipschitz maps do not increase Hausdorff measure by more than the factor Lip^k (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le) and Hᵏ = Lᵏ on ℝᵏ. Re-enumerate. Finally, replace M by M ∩ ⋃_iG_i(A_i) ((IMC)(b), E := ⋃_iG_i(A_i), Borel as a countable union of compact sets); the removed part is Hᵏ-null, so the represented current is still X, and now M = ⋃_iG_i(A_i) exactly (disjoint union).

8. B2 (Tangent planes of pieces; PT). For each i, PT (with F := G_i, B := A_i, L := Lip G_i, m := κ_i) gives: for Lᵏ-a.e. u ∈ A_i, range DG_i(u) is the approximate tangent space of G_i(A_i) at G_i(u).
 Jacobian bounds: JG_i(u) > 0 for every u ∈ A_i (DG_i(u) is injective), and JG_i(u) ≥ κ_iᵏ at every Lebesgue density point u of A_i, hence for a.e. u ∈ A_i (density gives points v ∈ A_i with v − u = rw/|w| + o(r) as r ↓ 0, so |DG_i(u)w| ≥ κ_i|w|, and (L3) gives JG_i(u) = √det(DG_i(u)ᵀDG_i(u)) ≥ κ_iᵏ). (Alternatively, G_i⁻¹ is (1/κ_i)-Lipschitz on G_i(A_i), so Lᵏ(S) ≤ κ_i^{−k}Hᵏ(G_i(S)) for S ⊆ A_i, which gives the integrability bound used in B3 directly.)
 Null sets correspond: if Z ⊆ G_i(A_i) has Hᵏ(Z) = 0 then Lᵏ({u ∈ A_i : G_i(u) ∈ Z}) = 0, because for a Borel Hᵏ-null Z' ⊇ Z (Borel regularity of Hᵏ), (AF) for G_i on the Borel set A_i ∩ G_i^{-1}(Z') gives ∫_{A_i∩G_i^{-1}(Z')}JG_i = Hᵏ(G_i(A_i) ∩ Z') = 0 while JG_i > 0 there. Conversely Lᵏ-null subsets of A_i have Hᵏ-null images (Lipschitz maps, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le).
 Consequence (B2′). By (IMC)(a) (G_i(A_i) ⊆ M Borel, Hᵏ(M) < ∞), for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ G_i(A_i), G_i(A_i) and M have the same approximate tangent spaces at x; by the IMRep property, for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space Q_x of M at x; approximate tangent spaces are unique when they exist (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Transferring null sets as above, for Lᵏ-a.e. u ∈ A_i: Q_{G_i(u)} = range DG_i(u) and, by (L3),
 ξ(G_i(u)) = s_i(u)Λ_kDG_i(u)(e)/JG_i(u), e := e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_k, s_i(u) ∈ {1, −1},
 where s_i is Borel: let τ(u) be the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization of DG_i(u)e_1, …, DG_i(u)e_k (Borel in u on A_i) and γ_u the k-covector v ↦ det(⟨τ_a(u), v_b⟩)_{a,b}; then Λ_kDG_i(u)(e)/JG_i(u) = τ_1(u) ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_k(u) (the change of frame is triangular with positive diagonal), so at the good points ξ(G_i(u))(γ_u) = ±1, and we put s_i(u) := 1 if ξ(G_i(u))(γ_u) ≥ 0 and s_i(u) := −1 otherwise (for every u ∈ A_i).

9. B3 (The integral formula is integer multiplicity). Let F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be Lipschitz and H_i := F ∘ G_i (Lipschitz on ℝᵏ). For Lipschitz H : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'}, w ∈ L¹(ℝᵏ) and ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(ℝ^{N'}) put
 I_H(w)(ω) := ∫ w(u)⟨ω(H(u)), Λ_kDH(u)(e)⟩ du,
 the integrand being taken where H is differentiable (Lᵏ-a.e., Rademacher: Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) and 0 elsewhere; |I_H(w)(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖Lip(H)ᵏ‖w‖₁ by (L1).
 Let w_i := (θ∘G_i)s_i1_{A_i}: it is integer-valued and integrable, since JG_i ≥ κ_iᵏ a.e. on A_i and, by (AF), ∫_{A_i}θ(G_iu)JG_i(u) du = ∫_{G_i(A_i)}θ dHᵏ < ∞. Where H_i and G_i are both differentiable at u ∈ A_i, |DH_i(u)w| = lim_{t↓0}|F(G_i(u + tw)) − F(G_i(u))|/t ≤ Lip F·|DG_i(u)w|, so DH_i(u) = A_u ∘ DG_i(u) with ‖A_u‖ ≤ Lip F on range DG_i(u), and |Λ_kDH_i(u)(e)| ≤ Lip(F)ᵏJG_i(u) by (L1). Hence |I_{H_i}(w_i)(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖Lip(F)ᵏ∫_{G_i(A_i)}θ dHᵏ, and
 Φ_F(ω) := Σ_i I_{H_i}(w_i)(ω)
 converges absolutely, with |Φ_F(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖Lip(F)ᵏM(X).
 Integrality. Where DH_i(u) is not injective, Λ_kDH_i(u)(e) = 0. Partition A_i^+ := {u ∈ A_i : H_i differentiable at u, DH_i(u) injective} (Borel) as in B1 (Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt and inner regularity) into countably many disjoint compact pieces A_{il}, up to an Lᵏ-null set, on which H_i is injective with |H_i(u) − H_i(v)| ≥ κ_{il}|u − v|, κ_{il} > 0. Put N_{il} := H_i(A_{il}) (compact), g_{il} := w_i∘(H_i|A_{il})^{-1} (integer-valued) and η_{il} := (Λ_kDH_i(e)/JH_i)∘(H_i|A_{il})^{-1}, a unit simple k-vector by (L3) (Borel: the inverse of a continuous injective map on a compact set is continuous). (AF) for H_i on A_{il} (with JH_i(u) = |Λ_kDH_i(u)(e)|) gives
 I_{H_i}(w_i1_{A_{il}})(ω) = ∫_{A_il} w_i⟨ω(H_i u), η_il(H_i u)⟩JH_i(u) du = Φ_{il}(ω) := ∫_{N_{il}} g_{il}⟨ω, η_{il}⟩ dHᵏ, and ∫_{N_{il}}|g_{il}| dHᵏ = ∫_{A_il}|w_i|JH_i ≤ Lip(F)ᵏ∫_{A_il}θ(G_iu)JG_i(u) du.
 Hence Φ_F(ω) = Σ_{i,l}Φ_{il}(ω) and Σ_{i,l}∫_{N_{il}}|g_{il}| dHᵏ ≤ Lip(F)ᵏM(X) < ∞.
 Each Φ_{il} is an integer multiplicity current, represented by the IMRep (N_{il}, |g_{il}|, sign(g_{il})η_{il}) (g_{il} never vanishes, since θ ≥ 1 on M and s_i = ±1; we write N'_{il} := N_{il}):
 - N'_{il} is Borel and countably k-rectifiable (a subset of the range of the Lipschitz map H_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'}), with Hᵏ(N'_{il}) ≤ ∫|g_{il}| < ∞;
 - the multiplicity is a positive integer, measurable and integrable, and the orientation is Borel;
 - by PT applied to H_i on A_{il} (H_i Lipschitz, bi-Lipschitz with constant κ_{il} on A_{il}, differentiable with injective derivative there), for Lᵏ-a.e. u ∈ A_{il} the approximate tangent space of N_{il} at H_i(u) is DH_i(u)(ℝᵏ), which η_{il}(H_i u) orients; by (IMC)(a) (N'_{il} ⊆ N_{il} Borel, Hᵏ(N_{il}) < ∞) and the correspondence of null sets of B2 (for H_i, A_{il}, κ_{il}), the same holds for N'_{il} at Hᵏ-a.e. point of N'_{il}.
 (Equivalently, the helper cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density from the candidate of IMS produces this IMRep from the integer density g_{il} on N_{il}.) Its action is Φ_{il}, it represents a current (dtc_imrep_current, or directly: |Φ_{il}(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖∫|g_{il}| gives sequential continuity), and M(Φ_{il}) ≤ ∫|g_{il}| dHᵏ (MR), so Σ_{il}M(Φ_{il}) < ∞. Enumerate the countably many pairs (i, l) by ℕ, padding with zero currents. IMS (degree k = (k − 1) + 1) gives an integer multiplicity current S with S(ω) = Σ_{il}Φ_{il}(ω) = Φ_F(ω) for every ω. Hence Φ_F is (the action of) an integer multiplicity current.

10. B4 (Identification F_#X = Φ_F).
 Lemma B4.1. Let H_σ, H : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'} (σ > 0) be L-Lipschitz with H_σ → H uniformly on ℝᵏ as σ ↓ 0. Then I_{H_σ}(w)(ω) → I_H(w)(ω) for every w ∈ L¹(ℝᵏ) and ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(ℝ^{N'}).
 Proof. (i) Reduction to smooth w. By the bound |I_{H'}(w)(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖Lᵏ‖w‖₁ for every L-Lipschitz H', it suffices to prove the claim for w in a subset of L¹(ℝᵏ) that is dense in L¹: an ε/3 argument then handles every w. C_c^∞(ℝᵏ) is dense in L¹(ℝᵏ): simple functions are dense in L¹ (Mathlib MemLp.exists_simpleFunc_eLpNorm_sub_lt); for a Borel set E of finite measure and ε > 0 there are a compact K ⊆ E and an open O ⊇ E with Lᵏ(O ∖ K) < ε (regularity of Lebesgue measure, Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_lt_add and Set.exists_isOpen_lt_add), and a continuous f : ℝᵏ → [0, 1] equal to 1 on K with compact support in O (Urysohn, Mathlib exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isCompact), so ‖1_E − f‖₁ < ε; finally f ∗ φ_δ ∈ C_c^∞ converges to f uniformly as δ ↓ 0 (uniform continuity of f) with supports in a fixed compact set, hence in L¹.
 (ii) For w ∈ C_c^∞(ℝᵏ) let S_w ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝᵏ), S_w(η) := ∫ w(u)η(u)(e) du. It is a current, spt S_w ⊆ spt w is compact, M(S_w) ≤ ∫|w| du, and for a (k − 1)-form η, writing η_j(u) := η(u)(e_1,…,ê_j,…,e_k), one has (dη)(u)(e) = Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}∂_jη_j(u), so integrating by parts ∂S_w(η) = S_w(dη) = −Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}∫∂_jw η_j du and M(∂S_w) ≤ ∫|∇w| du < ∞ (|Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}∂_jw η_j| ≤ |∇w||η|, the η_j being distinct coefficients of η) (for k = 1 this is the 0-current η ↦ −∫w'η). Thus S_w ∈ NC_k(ℝᵏ).
 (iii) For C^∞ maps H̃ : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'}, A1 gives H̃_#S_w(ω) = S_w(ζH̃^#ω) = ∫ w(u)(H̃^#ω)(u)(e) du = ∫ w⟨ω(H̃(u)), Λ_kDH̃(u)(e)⟩ du = I_{H̃}(w)(ω).
 (iv) For L-Lipschitz H let H_δ := H ∗ φ_δ (mollification on ℝᵏ as in A4). Then H_δ is C^∞, L-Lipschitz, H_δ → H uniformly, and DH_δ = (DH) ∗ φ_δ: differentiate under the integral sign (D(H ∗ φ_δ) = H ∗ Dφ_δ) and integrate by parts in each direction, which is legitimate for the Lipschitz H (Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq; the line derivative of H in direction v equals DH(u)v at every differentiability point). subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (1)–(25) (chapter-06.txt lines 1651–1843, printed pp. 163–166), with Lemma 5.4. The good centre, the retraction, the push-forward/homotopy calculus and the summation of integer multiplicity pieces are the sibling theorems cmcdt_good_center (GC), cmcdt_skeleton_retraction (RET), dtc_bc_tc_cl_dfm_lipschitz_pushforward_homotopy (PF) and cmcdt_im_series (IMS). Simon's currents T − T_ε are decomposed into dyadic shells (his (17)), and each shell is deformed with its own Lipschitz extension of ψ. Integrality of Q₀ and R₁ is obtained by summing the integer multiplicity shell contributions with IMS, in place of Simon's appeal to 3.13. The frozen statement is byte-identical to that of the leaf dtc_bc_lc_fd_dfm_skeleton_deformation (local_comparison branch, not accepted). Its dependencies RET, GC, PF and IMS have frozen types byte-identical to those of that leaf's dependencies; that leaf uses dtc_bc_lc_fd_dfm_skeleton_retraction and dtc_bc_lc_fd_dfm_lipschitz_pushforward_homotopy in place of RET and PF. So a fresh name is used, and an accepted single-theorem proof of that leaf can be transplanted after renaming RET and PF. The statement is that of cmcdt_skeleton_deformation (compactness_of_minimizing_currents branch, not yet accepted) except that the hypothesis REP is the representation theorem without the absolute-continuity clause (that clause is never used); the argument below is the one written and reviewed for that statement, with the choice of good radii (step 5) carried out with Stieltjes measures instead of the fundamental theorem of calculus for monotone functions, which is not in the frozen import closure.

Notation. n := m + 1. (VO), (MR), (REP), (IMC), (SL) are the five displayed hypotheses (frozen types of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support, Submission.cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, the sibling Submission.dtc_bc_lc_fd_dfm_mass_representation_core, Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub and Submission.cmc_slice_mass_bounds). All currents are on univ in ℝ^P. For currents A, B, “A + B” abbreviates A − (0 − B) (the contract's subtraction is pointwise, and currents are equal when their values agree, GeometricCurrentOn.ext). ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)|, and |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ for every current X. NC_k := k-currents with compact support, finite mass and (k ≥ 1) finite boundary mass; NC_k is closed under differences. Support facts used below (all from the definitions and (VO)): spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B; spt ∂A ⊆ spt A; spt 0 = ∅; a current that vanishes on every test form whose support is disjoint from a closed set E has support in E (every x ∉ E has a ball with compact closure disjoint from E). L_n := {x : ∃ s, P ≤ n + |s|, x_i ∈ ℤ (i ∈ s)} is closed (a finite union of the closed sets {x : x_i ∈ ℤ, i ∈ s}).

1. Trivial cases. If n ≥ P then L_n = ℝ^P (s = ∅). Take Q₀ := T, R₁ := 0, S₁ := 0 and c := 1: T − T − 0 = 0 = ∂0, T and 0 are integer multiplicity, the mass bounds are equalities or 0 ≤ ·, and spt T ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T), spt ∂T ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T), spt 0 = ∅. From now on n < P, so RET and GC apply. Let c_R > 0 be RET's constant, C_G := (GC's constant) + 1 > 0, c₄ := 8(1 + √P c_R), and
 c := max(1, c₄ⁿ(1 + 2C_G), √P 2ⁿ c₄ⁿ(1 + 2C_G), √P (2c₄)^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G), c₄^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)),
 which depends only on P and m. Let (push, homot) be the operators given by PF applied to (VO), (MR), (REP), (IMC). The zero current (in every degree) is integer multiplicity: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable, the remaining fields hold vacuously, and the representing integral over ∅ is 0). Let T be as in the statement. If M(T) = 0 then T = 0 (|T(ω)| ≤ M(T)‖ω‖), ∂T = 0, and Q₀ = R₁ = S₁ = 0 work. Assume M(T) > 0.

2. Measures. Let R_T = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of T and μ_T := R_T.measure. By (MR), μ_T(W) = M_W(T) for open W, so μ_T(ℝ^P) = M(T) < ∞, and μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = 0 by (VO). Further:
 - T(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ_T (definition of Represents and of the density measure);
 - ξ is μ_T-a.e. strongly measurable (μ_T ≪ Hⁿ⌞M);
 - |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ_T-a.e. by (IMC)(d);
 - μ_T is finite on compact sets.
 Since M(∂T) < ∞, (REP) (U = univ) gives μ_∂, ξ_∂ with μ_∂(W) = M_W(∂T) for open W, |ξ_∂| ≤ 1 and ∂T(η) = ∫ ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂; moreover μ_∂(ℝ^P) = M(∂T) and μ_∂(ℝ^P ∖ spt ∂T) = 0 by (VO).

3. Good centre (Simon (1)–(7); GC). GC applied to the finite measures μ_T, μ_∂ gives a with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 such that, for d := dist(·, L*(a)), L*(a) the set of y with at least m + 2 coordinates in a_i + ℤ,
 (6) μ_T({d < r}) ≤ C_G r^{n+1} M(T), (7) μ_∂({d < r}) ≤ C_G r^{n+1} M(∂T) for r ∈ (0, 1/4].
 In particular μ_T({d = 0}) = μ_∂({d = 0}) = 0.

4. Retraction (RET). RET with this a gives ψ with: if d(x) > 0 then ψ(x) ∈ L_n and |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P; and ψ is (c_R/r)-Lipschitz on {d ≥ r} for r ∈ (0, 1/4]. For r ∈ (0, 1/4] let φ_r be the componentwise McShane extension of ψ|{d ≥ r} (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real for each coordinate x ↦ ψ(x)_i, which is (c_R/r)-Lipschitz on {d ≥ r}). Then φ_r : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is (√P c_R/r)-Lipschitz and φ_r = ψ on {d ≥ r}. Put Λ(r) := max(1, √P c_R/r); id and φ_r are Λ(r)-Lipschitz, and Λ(r) ≤ c₄2^j whenever r ≥ 2^{−j−3}.

5. Slicing and good radii (Simon (8)–(10)). Apply (SL) with U = univ, k = m, T, μ := μ_T, μ' := μ_∂, ξ, ξ' := ξ_∂, f := d, L := 1 (d is 1-Lipschitz; the measures are finite on compact sets, and the a.e. bounds and representations hold by 2). This gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_n, B_t ∈ 𝒟_{n−1} with A_t(ω) = ∫_{d<t} ξ(ω) dμ_T, B_t(η) = ∫_{d<t} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂, ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) when tsupport η ∩ {d = t} = ∅, and, for Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t, M(Z_t) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h^{−1}μ_T({t − h < d < t}). If m ≥ 1, write m = k' + 1 and apply (SL) also to ∂T, which has degree k' + 1 (k := k' = m − 1, μ := μ_∂, ξ := ξ_∂, μ' := 0, ξ' := 0, valid because ∂∂T = 0; f := d). Its A'_t has the same values as B_t, so A'_t = B_t; its B'_t = 0; and M(∂B_t) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h^{−1}μ_∂({t − h < d < t}).
 Let G(t) := μ_T({d ≤ t}) and G_∂(t) := μ_∂({d ≤ t}) for t ∈ ℝ. They are nondecreasing, bounded and right-continuous (continuity from above of finite measures), i.e. Stieltjes functions, and their Stieltjes measures satisfy G.measure(Ioo(a, b)) = leftLim G b − G(a) = μ_T({a < d < b}) (Mathlib StieltjesFunction.measure_Ioo; leftLim G b = μ_T({d < b}) because {d ≤ b − 1/j} increases to {d < b} and finite measures are continuous from below), likewise for G_∂. By Mathlib StieltjesFunction.ae_hasDerivAt, for Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ ℝ the functions G and G_∂ are differentiable at t, with derivatives D(t) := (rnDeriv G.measure volume t).toReal and D_∂(t) := (rnDeriv G_∂.measure volume t).toReal. At such t, for h > 0, {t − h < d < t} ⊆ {t − h < d ≤ t}, so μ_T({t − h < d < t}) ≤ G(t) − G(t − h), i.e. ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_T({t − h < d < t}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal((G(t) − G(t − h))/h). Since G has derivative D(t) at t, the left difference quotients (G(t) − G(t − h))/h tend to D(t) as h ↓ 0, so the right side tends to ENNReal.ofReal(D(t)) along 𝓝[>] 0, and the liminf of the left side is at most ENNReal.ofReal(D(t)). Hence M(Z_t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(D(t)), and likewise M(∂B_t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(D_∂(t)) < ∞ (if m ≥ 1). (G and G_∂ are bundled as elements of StieltjesFunction ℝ: monotone and right-continuous.)
 For ν ≥ 0 let ρ_ν := 2^{−ν−2} ≤ 1/4. The density ρ ↦ rnDeriv G.measure volume ρ is measurable (Mathlib Measure.measurable_rnDeriv), and by Mathlib Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_le with withDensity_apply,
 ∫⁻_{Ioo(ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν)} rnDeriv G.measure volume dt ≤ G.measure(Ioo(ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν)) = μ_T({ρ_ν/2 < d < ρ_ν}) ≤ μ_T({d < ρ_ν}) ≤ C_G ρ_ν^{n+1} M(T)
 by (6). Put λ_ν := 4C_Gρ_νⁿM(T) > 0 (M(T) > 0 by step 1). By Markov's inequality (Mathlib mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀), the set of t ∈ (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) with rnDeriv G.measure volume t ≥ ENNReal.ofReal λ_ν has Lebesgue measure ≤ C_Gρ_ν^{n+1}M(T)/λ_ν = ρ_ν/4. As (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) has length ρ_ν/2 > ρ_ν/4 and the points where G or G_∂ is not differentiable form a null set, there is r_ν ∈ (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) at which G and G_∂ are differentiable and rnDeriv G.measure volume r_ν < ENNReal.ofReal λ_ν, so D(r_ν) ≤ λ_ν. Hence
 (10) M(Z_{r_ν}) ≤ 4C_Gρ_νⁿM(T) and M(∂B_{r_ν}) < ∞ (if m ≥ 1).
 (Simon also takes radii with μ_T({d = r_ν}) = 0; this is not needed below because the shells are taken half-open.)
 Since r_{ν+1} < ρ_{ν+1} = ρ_ν/2 < r_ν, the r_ν strictly decrease to 0, r_ν ≤ 1/4 and r_ν > 2^{−ν−3}. Write A_ν := A_{r_ν}, B_ν := B_{r_ν}, Z_ν := Z_{r_ν}.

6. The pieces (Simon (8), (17)). For j ≥ 0 define W_0 := T − A_0, W_j := A_{j−1} − A_j (j ≥ 1), D_0 := ∂T − B_0, D_j := B_{j−1} − B_j (j ≥ 1). Let E_0 := {d ≥ r_0} and E_j := {r_j ≤ d < r_{j−1}} (j ≥ 1).
 (6a) W_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ_T and D_j(η) = ∫_{E_j} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂. Hence M(W_0) ≤ M(T) and M(D_0) ≤ M(∂T), and for j ≥ 1, by (6), (7) with r_{j−1} < ρ_{j−1} = 2^{−j−1}: M(W_j) ≤ C_G 2^{−(j+1)(n+1)}M(T) and M(D_j) ≤ C_G 2^{−(j+1)(n+1)}M(∂T).
 (6b) W_j is integer multiplicity: (IMC)(b) with E := E_j gives a current represented by (M ∩ E_j, θ, ξ), whose values are ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ_T = W_j(ω).
 (6c) Supports: spt W_j ⊆ spt T ∩ closure(E_j) ⊆ spt T ∩ {d ≥ r_j} and spt D_j ⊆ spt ∂T ∩ {d ≥ r_j}. Indeed, if ω vanishes on spt T ∩ closure(E_j), the integrand of (6a) vanishes μ_T-a.e. on E_j (μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = 0), so W_j vanishes on forms supported off this closed set. spt Z_j ⊆ {d = r_j} by the third clause of (SL). Also spt A_t ⊆ spt T and spt B_t ⊆ spt ∂T ⊆ spt T, so all supports above are compact.
 (6d) Boundaries: ∂A_t = B_t + Z_t, hence ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0 and ∂W_j = D_j + Z_{j−1} − Z_j (j ≥ 1). For m ≥ 1, ∂D_0 = −∂B_0, ∂D_j = ∂B_{j−1} − ∂B_j and ∂Z_j = −∂B_j have finite mass by (10). Hence W_j ∈ NC_n and D_j, Z_j ∈ NC_{n−1} (for m = 0 there is no boundary condition in degree 0).
 (6e) Σ_{j=0}^{N} W_j = T − A_N and M(A_N) ≤ μ_T({d < r_N}) ≤ C_G ρ_N^{n+1}M(T) → 0.

7. Deforming the pieces (Simon (11)–(20)). For j ≥ 0 let φ_j := φ_{r_j} and Λ_j := Λ(r_j) ≤ c₄2^j (as r_j > 2^{−j−3}); Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}. Then φ_j = ψ on spt W_j ∪ spt D_j ∪ spt Z_j ⊆ {d ≥ r_j}, and φ_{j+1} = ψ = φ_j on spt Z_j ⊆ {d = r_j} ⊆ {d ≥ r_{j+1}}. Define
 V_j := push n φ_j W_j, H_j := homot n id φ_j W_j, Y_j := push (n−1) φ_j D_j, E'_j := homot (n−1) id φ_j D_j, L_j := push (n−1) φ_j Z_j, K_j := homot (n−1) id φ_j Z_j.
 - By PF (locality, maps Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz): push (n−1) φ_{j+1} Z_j = L_j and homot (n−1) id φ_{j+1} Z_j = K_j.
 - By PF (identity and homotopy formula in degree n = m + 1, with F = id, G = φ_j, Λ = Λ_j): V_j − W_j − homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_j) = ∂H_j.
 - By PF (linearity, all pieces in NC_{n−1}) and (6d): homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_0) = E'_0 − K_0 and homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_j) = E'_j + K_{j−1} − K_j (j ≥ 1).
 - By PF (boundary commutation and linearity): ∂V_0 = Y_0 − L_0 and ∂V_j = Y_j + L_{j−1} − L_j (j ≥ 1).
 Summing over j = 0,…,N (telescoping):
 (S1) Σ_{j≤N}(V_j − W_j − ∂H_j) = Σ_{j≤N}E'_j − K_N, (S2) ∂(Σ_{j≤N}V_j) = Σ_{j≤N}Y_j − L_N.
 W_j is integer multiplicity, so by the integrality clause of PF (degree k + 1 = n), push n φ_j W_j = V_j is integer multiplicity (with F := φ_j) and homot n id φ_j W_j = H_j is integer multiplicity (with F := id, G := φ_j).
 Estimates (PF mass bounds; |φ_j(x) − x| = |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P on the supports, since d > 0 there):
 M(V_0) ≤ c₄ⁿM(T), M(V_j) ≤ c₄ⁿ2^{jn}C_G2^{−(j+1)(n+1)}M(T) ≤ c₄ⁿC_G2^{−j}M(T);
 M(H_0) ≤ √P(2c₄)ⁿM(T), M(H_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)ⁿC_G2^{−j}M(T);
 M(Y_0) ≤ c₄^{n−1}M(∂T), M(Y_j) ≤ c₄^{n−1}C_G2^{−2j}M(∂T); M(E'_0) ≤ √P(2c₄)^{n−1}M(∂T), M(E'_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)^{n−1}C_G2^{−2j}M(∂T);
 M(L_N) ≤ Λ_{N}^{n−1}M(Z_N) ≤ c₄^{n−1}2^{N(n−1)}·4C_G2^{−(N+2)n}M(T) ≤ 4C_Gc₄^{n−1}2^{−N}M(T) → 0, and likewise M(K_N) ≤ √P(2Λ_N)^{n−1}M(Z_N) → 0.
 Hence Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ c₄ⁿ(1 + 2C_G)M(T), Σ_j M(H_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)ⁿ(1 + 2C_G)M(T), Σ_j M(E'_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)M(∂T) and Σ_j M(Y_j) ≤ c₄^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)M(∂T).

8. Limits (Simon (19)–(21), (24)–(25); IMS).
 - IMS (degree n = m + 1) gives Q₀ with Q₀(ω) = Σ_j V_j(ω): integer multiplicity, M(Q₀) ≤ Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ cM(T), spt Q₀ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt V_j.
 - By (IMC)(c), 0 − H_j is integer multiplicity (0 and H_j are), with M(0 − H_j) ≤ M(H_j). IMS (degree m + 2) gives R₁ with R₁(ζ) = Σ_j(0 − H_j)(ζ): integer multiplicity, M(R₁) ≤ cM(T), spt R₁ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt H_j.
 - IMS (degree m + 1, existence part) gives S₁ with S₁(ω) = Σ_j(0 − E'_j)(ω), M(S₁) ≤ cM(∂T), spt S₁ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt E'_j.
 Identity (21). Evaluate (S1) at ω: Σ_{j≤N}V_j(ω) − T(ω) + A_N(ω) − Σ_{j≤N}H_j(dω) = Σ_{j≤N}E'_j(ω) − K_N(ω). As N → ∞, A_N(ω) → 0 and K_N(ω) → 0 (masses → 0), so Q₀(ω) − T(ω) + R₁(dω) = −S₁(ω), i.e. (T − Q₀ − S₁)(ω) = ∂R₁(ω). Hence T − Q₀ − S₁ = R₁.boundary.
 Boundary mass (25). The finite sums Ŝ_N := Σ_{j≤N}V_j converge weakly to Q₀, so ∂Ŝ_N converge weakly to ∂Q₀ (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), and M(∂Q₀) ≤ liminf_N M(∂Ŝ_N) (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf). By (S2), M(∂Ŝ_N) ≤ Σ_jM(Y_j) + M(L_N), so M(∂Q₀) ≤ c₄^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)M(∂T) ≤ cM(∂T).

9. Supports (Simon (22)–(23)).
 - spt V_j ⊆ φ_j(spt W_j) = ψ(spt W_j) ⊆ L_n ∩ cthickening(√P, spt T) (RET, as d > 0 and the points lie in spt T). Both sets are closed, so spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n ∩ cthickening(√P, spt T).
 - spt H_j ⊆ {x + t(φ_j(x) − x) : x ∈ spt W_j, t ∈ [0,1]} ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T) (PF), so spt R₁ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T) (spt(0 − H_j) ⊆ spt H_j).
 - Likewise spt E'_j ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T), so spt S₁ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T).
 - Finally, if tsupport ω ∩ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T) = ∅, then Y_j(ω) = 0 for all j (spt Y_j ⊆ φ_j(spt D_j) ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T); (VO)). So ∂Ŝ_N(ω) = −L_N(ω) → 0 and ∂Q₀(ω) = lim ∂Ŝ_N(ω) = 0; hence spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T).

10. Q₀, R₁, S₁ satisfy all conclusions with the constant c of 1 (c ≥ 1): integrality (8), the identity (8), spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n (9), the four mass bounds (7)–(8) and the support inclusions (9). ∎
proof_key_steps: Trivial cases n ≥ P (Q₀ := T) and T = 0; constants from RET and GC.
